summary: Fractional token-metering delta after token-normalization update leading to invoice variance and missing provisional credit
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a consistent variance between expected token usage and invoiced token lines for several multi-day batches after our tokenizer normalization release (2026-03-08). The difference appears as fractional-token deltas that were not reconciled into provisional credits and show up as a small but persistent overcharge on their finalized invoice.

Impact:
- VectorAI Labs noticed ~0.6% higher token consumption on invoice lines for two billing days (2026-03-09 to 2026-03-10).
- Missing provisional credit prevented automatic mid-cycle correction; customer autopay charged the higher amount.
- Customer workload is production-critical; they flagged for finance reconciliation and requested a credit memo.

Environment:
- Dedicated account, reserved capacity, prod region us-east-1.
- Tokenization runtime rolled via tokenizer PR #412 on 2026-03-08 06:12 UTC.

Expected behavior:
- Token normalization change should not change aggregate billed token counts beyond rounding tolerance; fractional adjustments should be captured by hourly provisional credits and smoothing.

Actual behavior:
- Metering pipeline recorded fractional token amounts (e.g., 1034.6 tokens) that were truncated at later aggregation steps leading to a net +0.6% overreport. Provisional credit reconciliation skipped those small deltas due to an edge-case filter in the reconcilier (min_delta >= 1.0 tokens).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use tokenizer v2.11 normalization (PR #412) to encode a corpus with many accentuated unicode sequences.
2) Send streaming requests to the hosted API and capture per-request token counts from /v1/usage hooks.
3) Let the usage-postback-processor batch hourly and run the reconcilier job.
4) Observe aggregated hourly lines; compare with previous tokenizer baseline and note fractional deltas not turned into provisional credits.
logs:
Sample postback snippet (anonymized):
- request_id: req-9af3b2, raw_tokens: 1034.6, recorded_tokens: 1035, postback_aggregate_hour: 2026-03-09T18:00Z
- reconciler log: INFO reconciler/hourly - delta=0.6 tokens, ignoring delta < 1.0 per config 'min_credit_delta_tokens'
- billing pipeline: billed_tokens=1035, provisional_adjustments=0
Stack traces: none (no runtime exceptions).
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support found correlation with tokenizer PR #412 that changed Unicode normalization (NFKC tweak) and whitespace collapse rules. Engineering repro shows per-request fractional tokens appear when normalizing combined accent sequences; previous tokenizer produced integer token counts per request in same corpus.
Billing team confirmed the reconciler intentionally ignores fractional deltas under 1.0 tokens to avoid noisy credits (historical heuristic) — this was never revisited after token-counts became fractional.
Preliminary math for VectorAI sample window (2026-03-09):
- raw billed tokens (post-PR): 1,205,340
- raw billed tokens (pre-PR baseline): 1,197,480
- observed delta: +7,860 tokens (~0.66%)
- Delta caused by many small fractional increments across millions of requests; aggregated rounding bias accumulated.
Hypothesis: tokenizer change introduced systematic fractionalization which the postback aggregation truncates up, causing net positive bias. Reconciler filter prevented provisional credits from being applied.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Support issued a provisional credit for the affected window equal to estimated delta ($1,230) and blocked autopay retry until credit memo accepted by customer. Engineering action: rolled back tokenizer normalization change on dedicated clusters for VectorAI on 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC to eliminate new fractional behavior. Billing fixes: raised a ticket to update reconciler threshold to min_credit_delta_tokens=0.1 and add fractional-aware aggregation in billing PR #89.
Follow-up actions planned: 1) Reprocess affected postbacks for 2026-03-08 through 2026-03-10 with corrected aggregation and issue formal credit memo. 2) Add unit tests to tokenizer to assert integer-preserving metering invariants for common corpora. 3) Postmortem scheduled and link will be added to this ticket.
